name: How much more does an attached ADU cost than a garage conversion?

mainEntity.name: Is an attached ADU usually more expensive than converting a garage, and what drives the price difference?
mainEntity.text: Is an attached ADU usually more expensive than converting a garage, and what drives the price difference?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached ADU usually costs more than a garage conversion because it is closer to building a new addition than converting an existing shell. The biggest cost drivers are foundation work, new framing, roof integration, insulation, windows, exterior finishes, and utility extensions. Garage conversions can sometimes save money because the structure already exists, but they may also bring hidden costs if the slab is weak, the garage needs seismic reinforcement, or the roof height is too low for comfortable living. Attached ADUs sit in the middle: they are often more expensive than a straightforward conversion but can be cheaper than a fully detached new build because one or more walls may tie into the existing house. The right comparison depends on the site, not just the unit type. Homeowners should compare all-in costs, including design, permits, utility upgrades, and contingency, rather than only construction price per square foot. The cheapest option on paper is not always the most practical or highest-value use of the property.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, an attached ADU usually costs more than a garage conversion because it often requires new foundation work, framing, roofing, insulation, windows, and utility tie-ins. Garage conversions are often cheaper because they reuse an existing shell, while attached additions are closer to full construction.
